misconceptions.description: Writing a Design Tension Studio map that names only the benefit axis (for example feedback speed) and leaves the competing value (authorship, teacher judgment) off the map
misconceptions.trigger: facilitator note recommends a tool without naming the value it trades against
misconceptions.feedback: A tension map needs both axes. Name the competing value the tool puts at risk, not only the benefit it offers.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a technology choice carries the same risk for every student instead of locating who bears the equity cost (ELL students, students with IEPs)
misconceptions.trigger: note describes the class as a single group with no subgroup risk
misconceptions.feedback: Locate who bears the risk. Name the specific students for whom the tool is most likely to misfire.

misconceptions.description: Logging that the team liked or chose a tool rather than recording the negotiated decision the team can be held to and later test
misconceptions.trigger: map ends with a preference and no commitment or evidence plan
misconceptions.feedback: Record the negotiated decision and what evidence would later confirm it, not just which tool the team preferred.

misconceptions.description: Defending a classroom tool because it is engaging rather than because it protects students and improves a specific learning activity
misconceptions.trigger: the only stated reason for the tool is that students find it fun
misconceptions.feedback: Engagement is not a justification on its own. Tie the choice to a protected learning value and a named risk.
